name: Margaret Halloran
background: Margaret Halloran leads the state government, which will be held responsible for whatever the state decides on the pending Redpoll Ridge Project. She weighs mining jobs and state revenue against the opposition to the Manh Choh ore haul heard at the 2024 public meetings, and she sets the state's line on mining tax.

name: Douglas Renfrew
role: Commissioner, Alaska Department of Natural Resources (DNR)
background: Douglas Renfrew heads the DNR, which approved the reclamation plan Manh Choh operates under and must now decide on the Redpoll Ridge Project application. He looks at how a mining approval would affect state revenue, jobs and local opposition.

name: Evelyn Marchetti
background: Evelyn Marchetti runs the DNR division that reviews mine plans and reclamation. Manh Choh operates under a DNR-approved reclamation plan, and her division's review of the pending Redpoll Ridge Project application will feed into the DNR decision.

name: Raymond Takahashi
role: Alaska state director, Bureau of Land Management (BLM)
background: Raymond Takahashi leads the federal Bureau of Land Management (BLM) in Alaska. Manh Choh sits entirely on Native Village of Tetlin land, not federal land, but he tracks whether new mining near Tok, including the Redpoll Ridge Project, would touch federal land or need federal permits.

name: Curtis Lindqvist
role: State legislator for the Tok district
background: Curtis Lindqvist represents Tok in the Alaska Legislature. Mine jobs and local business matter in his district, and so do the complaints about pavement damage, safety and the environment raised at the 2024 meetings on the ore haul. He will be expected to take a public side on the Redpoll Ridge Project.

name: Naomi Crane
background: Naomi Crane is a state tax official who works on Alaska's tax on mining. She estimates what a higher gold price or a change in the tax rate would bring in from mines such as Manh Choh, and she would draft the details of any proposal to raise the tax on gold mining.

name: Gordon Strand
role: Regional director, Alaska Department of Transportation (DOT), for the ore-haul highway
background: Gordon Strand is responsible for the state highways the Manh Choh ore haul uses. With about 60 round trips a day of 95-foot ore trucks running to the Fort Knox mill, his office handles the pavement damage, maintenance costs and safety questions that the haul raises.

name: Alicia Mendoza
role: Regional official, Alaska Department of Environmental Conservation (DEC), water
background: Alicia Mendoza works on water quality for the DEC in the region around Tok. She follows water questions around Manh Choh and would be involved in reviewing the water side of the Redpoll Ridge Project.

name: Kyle Brannigan
background: Kyle Brannigan carries out field inspections of mine sites for the DNR, including Manh Choh. He checks that mines follow their approved reclamation plans, and his findings feed the DNR's view of new mines such as the Redpoll Ridge Project.

name: Walter Sobczak
background: Walter Sobczak supervises state highway maintenance out of Tok. The ore trucks bound for the Fort Knox mill add wear to the pavement he repairs, and he deals first hand with the maintenance costs raised at the 2024 public meetings.

name: Diane Kessler
background: Diane Kessler runs Manh Choh for Kinross, the mine's operator and 70% owner. She answers for its about 300 employees, the 141,000 ounces of gold it produced in 2024 and the ore haul to the Fort Knox mill. How the state handles the Redpoll Ridge Project matters to Kinross's plans in Alaska.

name: Vernon Ostrander
background: Vernon Ostrander is chief of the Native Village of Tetlin council. Manh Choh sits entirely on Tetlin land, and the village owns the surface and mineral rights and leases them to Peak Gold LLC. He weighs lease income and jobs for the village against protecting its land and water.

name: Sharon Delancey
background: Sharon Delancey represents a regional Alaska Native corporation in the Interior. She looks for jobs and contract work from Manh Choh and any new mine near Tok, and she also hears concerns about land and subsistence from villages in the region.

name: Brent Holloway
background: Brent Holloway manages the trucking contractor that hauls Manh Choh ore about 240 miles to the Fort Knox mill. He runs about 60 round trips a day with B-train trucks about 95 feet long, and his contract depends on the haul staying open and on answering the safety complaints.

name: Marcus Delgado
background: Marcus Delgado is a crew lead at Manh Choh. Mining there began in late 2023 and is expected to last 4 to 5 years, so he already wonders where the next job will come from, and the Redpoll Ridge Project could be it.

name: Tanya Rasmussen
background: Tanya Rasmussen operates heavy equipment at Manh Choh and lives in Tok. She sees the mine job as the best-paid work she can get near home, and she follows the gold price because she believes it decides how long mining near Tok will last.

name: Jesse Pellerin
background: Jesse Pellerin works rotations at Manh Choh and lives in Fairbanks between shifts. With Manh Choh expected to finish mining after 4 to 5 years, he wants to know whether the Redpoll Ridge Project will be approved.

name: Dale Merritt
background: Dale Merritt drives a B-train ore truck from Manh Choh to the Fort Knox mill, about 240 miles each way. The haul is his income, and he hears the complaints about truck safety from people along the route.

name: Ricky Santoro
background: Ricky Santoro drives ore trucks on the Manh Choh haul to the Fort Knox mill and is new to the job. He moved north for the pay and would stay if more mining near Tok kept him working.

name: Ingrid Solberg
background: Ingrid Solberg works at the Fort Knox mill near Fairbanks, which processes the ore trucked in from Manh Choh. Her job depends on a steady supply of ore, so she follows the haul and any new mine near Tok.

name: Gloria Purcell
role: Fuel and supply business owner, Tok
background: Gloria Purcell owns a fuel and supply business in Tok. Her sales have grown with the mine and the ore-haul traffic, and she would gain from the Redpoll Ridge Project, but she also hears local complaints about the trucks at her counter.

name: Clayton Ruud
background: Clayton Ruud works a small family placer gold claim in the Tok area. A higher gold price makes his claim pay better and he backs mining in general, but he does not want large mines to tie up land or water that small miners use.

name: Wade Tillotson
background: Wade Tillotson runs a seasonal placer mining operation near Tok and sells his gold at market prices, so every move in the gold price changes his season. He watches the state's decision on the Redpoll Ridge Project for what it means for mining permits near Tok.

name: Patricia Engstrom
background: Patricia Engstrom chairs the Tok community council. She has to balance residents who want mine jobs and business against those who opposed the ore haul at the 2024 public meeting in Tok, and the council will be asked for a position on the Redpoll Ridge Project.

name: Lorraine Pike
role: Road-safety campaigner on the ore-haul route
background: Lorraine Pike lives on the ore-haul route and campaigns for road safety. About 60 round trips a day of 95-foot ore trucks pass near her home, and since the 2024 public meetings she has pushed for safer trucking or alternatives to trucking.

name: Miriam Castellanos
background: Miriam Castellanos leads a local environmental group based in Tok. Her focus is water, wildlife and land around Tok and Tetlin, and she is preparing objections to the Redpoll Ridge Project application.

name: Frank Abernathy
role: Lodge owner on the Alaska Highway
background: Frank Abernathy runs a lodge on the Alaska Highway near Tok. Mine workers and contractors fill some of his rooms, but ore-truck traffic and road wear bother his tourist guests, so the mine both helps and hurts his business.

name: Samuel Ahlberg
background: Samuel Ahlberg hunts and fishes around Tok to feed his family. He cares most about the land, water and wildlife near Manh Choh and the proposed Redpoll Ridge Project, and about keeping access to the places he hunts.

name: Debra Quintana
background: Debra Quintana drives a school bus in Tok and shares the road with ore-haul trucks. Road safety on the school runs is her first concern, though she knows Manh Choh brings jobs to Tok.

name: Heather Moravec
background: Heather Moravec is raising two children in Tok. She wants good jobs that keep young families in town, and she also wants clean water and safe roads for her children.

name: Julian Westbrook
role: Chief investment officer, largest gold macro hedge fund
background: Julian Westbrook runs the macro hedge fund with the largest gold position among its peers. He trades gold on central bank policy, the dollar and inflation, and he follows gold supply, including mines such as Manh Choh, when he sizes the position.

name: Priya Raghunathan
role: Head of the largest gold ETF
background: Priya Raghunathan runs the largest gold exchange-traded fund (ETF). Investor money flowing in or out changes how much physical gold the fund holds, and she watches the gold price and mining news for what moves those flows.

name: Oliver Brandt
background: Oliver Brandt manages a mining-equity fund that holds large gold producers, including Kinross. Manh Choh's output and any approval of the Redpoll Ridge Project bear on the value of the companies he holds.

name: Sofia Varga
background: Sofia Varga manages a mining-equity fund focused on North American gold producers. She compares mines on cost, mine life and permitting risk, and she treats Alaska's decision on the Redpoll Ridge Project as a test of permitting risk in the state.

name: Kenneth Mwangi
background: Kenneth Mwangi manages a mining-equity fund that holds stakes in gold producers and mine partners, including Contango ORE. Changes in Alaska's mining tax or permitting feed straight into his valuations.

name: Victor Hale
background: Victor Hale runs a trend-following fund, a commodity trading advisor (CTA), that trades gold futures on systematic signals. His models add to positions when prices break out and cut them when trends turn, so a gold breakout moves his book directly.

name: Elena Varnum
background: Elena Varnum manages a fund that positions around central bank buying and selling of gold. She tracks official reserve flows and policy statements, and she sees mine supply such as Manh Choh's mainly as a backdrop to those flows.

name: Robert Glenning
background: Robert Glenning decides how much of a large pension fund goes into gold and gold miners. He looks at gold as a hedge for the fund's long-term obligations and follows mining and tax policy in states such as Alaska.

name: Hannah Whitcombe
role: Head of a bullion bank desk
background: Hannah Whitcombe runs the precious metals desk at a bullion bank, making markets in physical gold and gold futures. She sees shifts in physical demand directly through her desk and follows supply news from producers such as Kinross.

name: Tyler Brockman
background: Tyler Brockman runs a fund that invests in junior gold explorers and developers. A project like the Redpoll Ridge Project is the kind of asset his fund looks for, so the state's decision on it matters to how he values similar projects.

name: Amara Osei
background: Amara Osei manages a junior-miner fund focused on early-stage gold projects in Alaska and Canada. Permitting decisions in Alaska set the value of the undeveloped deposits her fund is exposed to, so she follows the Redpoll Ridge Project application.

name: Leo Zhang
background: Leo Zhang runs a quantitative momentum fund that trades gold, gold miners and gold ETFs on price and volume signals. A gold breakout feeds straight into his models, and he pays attention to local mining news only when it moves prices.

name: Charlotte Vandermeer
background: Charlotte Vandermeer manages a family office that has held physical gold for decades. She sees gold as a store of family wealth across generations and looks at mining companies when their valuations stand out.

name: Farid Haddad
background: Farid Haddad invests for a family office whose fortune came from mining. He holds gold and shares in North American producers, and he follows Alaska's mining politics because permitting can make or break a mine.

name: Beatrice Lowell
background: Beatrice Lowell is chief investment officer of a family office that splits its gold exposure between bullion and royalty companies. She reads every new mine and tax change in places like Alaska for its effect on long-term returns.

name: Simon Archer
background: Simon Archer manages a long-only gold fund that holds bullion and large gold miners and never sells short. A higher gold price lifts his fund directly, and he follows Manh Choh and Kinross as part of his miner holdings.

name: Nadia Kovacs
background: Nadia Kovacs runs a long-only fund invested in gold mining companies of all sizes. She follows Alaska as a mining region, including Manh Choh and the pending Redpoll Ridge Project.

name: Daniel Ferreira
background: Daniel Ferreira runs the commodities book at a multi-strategy fund. Gold is one of many positions he can grow or shrink, and he trades gold against mining shares when news such as a mine approval or a tax change pulls them apart.

name: Grace Thornbury
background: Grace Thornbury is a portfolio manager at a multi-strategy fund covering metals and mining shares. She trades around company and policy news, including Kinross results and permitting decisions in Alaska.

name: Ian Rothman
background: Ian Rothman oversees risk at a multi-strategy fund that holds gold through futures and ETFs. He judges whether a gold breakout rests on real demand or short-term flows, and he sets how much gold exposure the fund keeps.

name: Mateo Alvarez
background: Mateo Alvarez trades gold futures and options on a commodity trading desk. He reads central bank comments, economic data and mining news for their effect on the gold price.

name: Rebecca Sterling
role: Head of a commodity trading desk
background: Rebecca Sterling runs a commodity trading desk that buys and sells physical gold from producers and refiners. Supply news from mines such as Manh Choh is part of her daily business, alongside the gold price itself.

name: Howard Prentiss
background: Howard Prentiss manages a risk-parity fund that spreads risk across stocks, bonds, commodities and gold. When gold becomes more volatile his rules cut the position, so a breakout changes his holdings even without a view on mining.

name: Yuki Tanabe
background: Yuki Tanabe co-manages a risk-parity fund that holds gold as one of its main diversifying assets. She rebalances as prices move and follows mining supply and policy news for its effect on gold volatility.

name: Shirley Dombrowski
background: Shirley Dombrowski is a retired teacher who keeps part of her retirement savings in gold coins and a gold ETF. She reads gold and mining news to decide whether to keep or sell her gold.

name: Kevin Marsh
background: Kevin Marsh is an electrician who invests a set amount each month in index funds and a gold mining ETF. He follows the gold price and news about mining companies such as Kinross.

name: Angela Fortier
background: Angela Fortier is a nurse who holds a gold ETF and a few mining shares in her retirement account. She follows the gold price and news about mining in Alaska.

name: Tyrone Weller
background: Tyrone Weller trades gold futures and gold mining shares from home. He buys what is rising and sells what is falling, and a gold breakout is exactly the setup he trades.

name: Brianna Costa
background: Brianna Costa trades options on gold ETFs and junior mining shares. Big price moves and mining news such as approvals or court rulings are her trading opportunities.

name: Dylan Hargrove
background: Dylan Hargrove is a part-time trader who trades gold and silver futures on price charts. News about mines near Tok matters to him only when it moves the price.

name: Tok River News Wire
background: Tok River News Wire is a local news outlet covering Tok, Manh Choh, the ore haul and the gold market. It publishes news reports only and does not take sides.
